Risk: Two SQL trees with divergent same-name slices
Evidence: deploy/sql (57) and CrossBuy/deploy/sql (60); 4 filenames in both, all 4 differ, 0 identical. manifest.json already records all 4 with identical=false and distinctHashes=2.
Impact: 'Apply pos_setup.sql' is ambiguous - the manifest states this explicitly.
Mitigation: D-38 names a canonical root; D-39 reconciles each pair deliberately in R1. No file moved in this increment.

Evidence: platform_schema_history.sql is authored but applied nowhere. manifest.json answers the AUTHORED side (115 scripts, SHA-256, apply rank) but has no database-side counterpart.
Impact: No reliable answer to 'which slices are applied to this database'.
Mitigation: D-40: PlatformSchemaHistory as the applied registry, first slice in every environment.

Risk: Kernel is a hard runtime dependency
Evidence: RecordAsync has no swallowing catch; ReverseAsync depends on BusinessEvents.
Impact: A missing table fails a real sale or any correction.
Mitigation: Every platform slice applied and verified before each phase.

Evidence: The kernel requires a signed-in context; a new background writer would throw.
Impact: A future background document writer fails in production.
Mitigation: Covered by the DI wiring test; re-checked on every new hosted service.

Evidence: PlatformOpsAttribute falls back to Accounting.manage.
Impact: Platform operations granted through an accounting role.
Mitigation: Closed - Accounting.manage is Never-bootstrap-open, asserted directly.

Evidence: Mutation H first passed against a stale assembly under --no-build.
Impact: Evidence that proves nothing.

Risk: Three platforms with no user reach
Evidence: Reporting, Communication and Construction C1: 533 tests, 34 tables, 0 screens.
Impact: Stakeholders may believe features exist.
Mitigation: Catalog separates CurrentStatus from ProductionActivation and UIStatus; R2-R4 convert them.

Evidence: AI services exist with no AI-specific authorization; no search exists.
Impact: AI surfaces data a user may not access.
Mitigation: Route AI through the reporting dataset layer (D-27).

Evidence: No MDM; Employee, Customer, Item and Supplier shared informally.
Impact: Duplicate and divergent master records.
Mitigation: Per-entity ownership register in R6 (D-31).

Risk: An unreviewed script is in the tree
Evidence: manifest.json classifies hm16_rename_grni.sql as 'review' - a mutating batch with no re-run guard that nobody has read - and script.sql as 'not-deployable'.
Impact: A re-run could mutate data unguarded, or a deployment could include a script judged unsafe.
Mitigation: Resolve or formally exclude both before any environment promotion (R1).

Risk: Provisioning does not use the slices at all
Evidence: deploy/README.md states the authoritative way to stand up the schema is BACKUP/RESTORE of CrossBuyDB2, because EF migrations are broken and ~90 ad-hoc scripts in C:/temp built the schema - a third source outside the repository.
Impact: The slice registry describes a build path that is not the one actually used; a fresh environment may not match any manifest state.
Mitigation: R1 must reconcile the restore-based path with the slice registry and decide which is authoritative for new environments.

Risk: Workspace could become a permission bypass
Evidence: A unified surface aggregating cross-module data is the classic place for an authorization shortcut.
Impact: One aggregated query could return data the user cannot see in the owning module.
Mitigation: D-41: Workspace adds NO permissions; every read delegates to the owning module's access service. Per-module delegation tests are an R3 gate.

Risk: Brand divergence between spec and code
Evidence: D-36 makes CrossBusiness Blue canonical while crossbuy-brand.css globally overrides to green and gold across 327 views.
Impact: New and legacy screens look like two products.
Mitigation: D-37 rollout: blue on new screens first, legacy migrated through an approved visual rollout.
